theater: 巴克特里亞東境扎拉夫尚河谷

battle.name: 遊牧民族入侵巴克特里亞
battle.theater: 巴克特里亞東境扎拉夫尚河谷
battle.brief: 前162年前後，塞種等遊牧部眾在匈奴西推與大月氏西遷的連鎖壓力下向西南移動，進抵巴克特里亞東境扎拉夫尚河谷，焚掠城邑。歐克拉提德一世自巴克特拉出兵，以巴克特里亞弓騎與重裝騎兵迎戰，據古典摘錄載擊退來敵，然戰果無數目可核。本戰記載簡略，經過只能由尤斯丁的摘錄、錢幣與漢籍推得。

kit.name: 亞述長弓
kit.history: 亞述人靠弓和鐵的組合征服兩河流域。弓兵在車上射，車兵靠弓兵開路。

countries: 交戰的兩方，一方是塞種人（Saka、塞薩），即古典作家筆下自雅克薩特斯河對岸而來的草原聯盟；另一方是歐克拉提德王朝治下的希臘化巴克特里亞王國。塞種並非單一民族，而是費爾干納、伊犁河谷與天山南北諸部落的聯盟，平日按部落分牧，遇戰由各部首領臨時集結，沒有固定王號，沒有常備軍，也沒有攻城器械；其戰力核心是全射擊的騎兵，裝備貼身自帶的短反曲弓與骨飾馬具，作戰目標是牧場、越冬地與掠奪所得，而非佔領城市。巴克特里亞一方則是典型的希臘化王權：以巴克特拉（Bactra，今阿富汗 Balkh）為都，國王歐克拉提德一世是全軍最高統帥，下設總督與各路將領，兵源混合了馬其頓—希臘移民後裔、本地巴克特里亞人、索格底亞人，以及招募來的斯基泰與達赫傭兵；軍隊骨幹是巴克特里亞式的弓騎大軍與重裝騎兵，東面亞伊哈努姆一線還有希臘化的城與堡壘。第三方並未直接參戰，但壓力來自兩面：北面是匈奴西推而南移的大月氏與塞種，西面是帕提亞王國自米特里達特一世以降向北吞併河中，把游牧勢力整體擠向巴克特里亞。
countriesEn: The two sides were the Saka (Saka, or Sacaraucae) and the Sacae of the classical writers, a steppe confederation that came from beyond the Jaxartes, and the Hellenistic kingdom of Bactria under the Eucratid dynasty. The Saka were not a single people but a confederation of tribes from Ferghana, the Ili valley and both sides of the Tian Shan; they grazed in separate tribal herds in peacetime and in war mustered only as each chief's following came together, with no fixed royal title, no standing army and no siege engines of any kind. Their fighting core was a wholly missile-armed mounted force, carrying a short reflex bow and bone-decorated horse gear, and their objectives were pasture, winter quarters and the spoils of plunder rather than the holding of cities. The Bactrian side was a typical Hellenistic kingship: capital at Bactra (Bactra, modern Balkh in Afghanistan), with the king, Eucratides I, as supreme commander of the whole army and satraps and divisional commanders beneath him. Its troops were mixed: descendants of Macedonian and Greek settlers, local Bactrians, Sogdians, and recruited Scythian and Dahae mercenaries. The backbone of the force was the Bactrian-style mass of mounted archers together with cataphracts, and along the eastern line lay the Hellenistic cities and forts of the Ai-Khanoum region. No third party fought in the battle, but the pressure came from two directions: from the north, the Yuezhi and the Saka pushed south by the Xiongnu, and from the west, the Parthian kingdom, which under Mithridates I and his successors gobbled up the lands between the Oxus and the Jaxartes and pressed the nomadic powers bodily against Bactria.
people: 留下姓名的，是巴克特里亞方面的統治者。歐克拉提德一世（Eucratides I，約前171年至前145年在位）是公元前二世紀上半葉中亞最強悍的君主之一，他約在前171年以政變推翻狄俄多托斯與歐提德莫斯一系，建立歐克拉提德王朝，並在錢幣上以自己的肖像取代亞歷山大大帝的頭像，頭銜寫作「偉大」（Μέγας），這在整個希臘化世界是絕無僅例的做法；他在位期間東征印度，與印度—希臘諸王交戰，也曾兩度迎擊北方來敵。敘述這一段的主要史料是三世紀的尤斯丁（Marcus Junianus Justinus）所編《腓史簡編》第十一卷，該書以龐普尼奧斯·特羅古斯的《史前紀》為底本；此外有斯特拉波第十一卷的地理記載，以及狄奧多若斯書稿的殘篇。中國方面的平行記載是《史記·大宛列傳》與《漢書·西域傳》中張騫所述的大月氏與塞種，包括大月氏「控弦之士十餘萬」與大夏「城邑數百」的數目。遊牧一方沒有留下首領的名字，這本身就是重要事實：古典文獻只以族名稱之，如老普林尼《自然史》第六卷所記的阿西人、帕西安人、吐火羅與薩卡勞伊。歐克拉提德晚年可能死於自己人或地方總督之手，約前145年，其子希羅克拉底斯一世成為巴克特里亞最後一位希臘王。
peopleEn: The names that survive belong to the rulers of Bactria. Eucratides I (Eucratides I, on the throne roughly 171 to 145 BC) was among the most formidable monarchs of Central Asia in the first half of the second century BC. Around 171 BC he seized power by coup, overthrowing the line of Diodotus and Euthydemes, and founded the Eucratid dynasty; on his coinage he put his own portrait in place of the head of Alexander the Great and styled himself 'the Great' (Megas), an act without parallel anywhere in the Hellenistic world. During his reign he campaigned into India, fought the Indo-Greek kings, and twice met the enemy coming from the north. The principal narrative source for this stretch is the eleventh book of the Epitome of Pompeius Trogus compiled in the third century by Marcus Junianus Justinus; to this are added the geographical account of Strabo in book eleven and the fragments of Diodorus. The Chinese parallel record is the Shiji chapter on Dayuan and the Hanshu chapter on the Western Regions, where Zhang Qian reports on the Yuezhi and the Saka, including the figures of more than a hundred thousand bowmen of the Yuezhi and several hundred cities in Daxia. The nomads left no name for their leaders, and that is itself an important fact: the classical writers name them only by tribal designations, such as the Asii, Pasiani, Tochari and Sacarauli listed in the sixth book of Pliny the Elder's Natural History. Eucratides may have been killed late in his reign by one of his own men or by a provincial satrap, around 145 BC, after which his son Heliocles I became the last Greek king to rule in Bactria.
kits: 卡面這件亞述長弓是公元前七世紀新亞述帝國的制式武器：角、筋、木三層貼合的複合弓，弓身長逾一米二，拉距約七十至八十厘米，箭長約九十厘米，箭鏃用燧石或青銅。它的用法是成排齊射，亞述弓兵站在輕型戰車上或步兵陣線後方，以輪射壓倒前排，戰車則以弓兵開路、衝鋒兵收尾。這件武器在公元前一六二年早已退出現役，新亞述王國在前七世紀末就已覆滅，但它所代表的技術血統恰恰就是當年交戰雙方所用的武器。塞種人使用約六十至七十厘米的短反曲弓，角木複合、三段反曲，張力大而可行至約兩百米，箭為短而重的箭，配骨鏽或鐵鏽，數十支束在兼作箭袋的皮囊裡；巴克特里亞與帕提亞一方使用較長的角筋木角弓與希臘式彎弓，弓兵以散射而非齊射作戰，並有小型弩與石弩可用。雙方其他裝備同樣可以對照：希臘化巴克特里亞有馬其頓式薩里沙長矛、方陣重步兵裝備、重裝騎兵的鱗甲與胸甲，以及安息式輕裝戰車；塞種人只有短刀、獸皮甲、柳條或木盾，沒有戰車，也沒有攻城塔與撞槌。馬具上，塞種馬用骨飾馬銜與環形頸環，還沒有馬鐙。
kitsEn: The Assyrian bow on the card is the standard weapon of the Neo-Assyrian empire of the seventh century BC: a composite bow of horn, sinew and wood, more than a metre and a quarter along the limbs, drawing to some seventy or eighty centimetres, with arrows about ninety centimetres long and flint or bronze heads. Its use was massed volley fire, Assyrian archers shooting from light chariots or from behind the infantry line to crush the enemy front, the chariots themselves being opened and closed by the bowmen. This weapon had long been out of service by 162 BC, the Neo-Assyrian kingdom having collapsed at the end of the seventh century, yet the technical tradition it represents was precisely the tradition in the hands of both sides in 162. The Saka used a short reflex bow of some sixty to seventy centimetres, a horn-and-wood composite with three recurved sections, powerful enough to shoot to roughly two hundred metres, with short heavy arrows carrying bone or iron heads, dozens of them kept in a skin case that doubled as a quiver. The Bactrian and Parthian side used longer horn-and-sinew angular bows and Greek-style curved bows, their archers firing loose rather than in volley, and had small crossbows and stone-throwers available. Other equipment can be compared as well: Hellenistic Bactria had the Macedonian sarissa, the equipment of heavy phalanx infantry, lamellar and scale armour for the cataphracts, and light Parthian-style chariots. The Saka had only a short knife, hide armour, and wicker or wooden shields, no chariots, and no siege towers or rams. On the horse tack the Saka horse carried bone-decorated bits and ring-shaped neck ornaments, and stirrups were not yet in use.
tactics: 兩家的戰術體系幾乎是相反的。塞種的戰法不攻城、不佔城，兵鋒直指牧場與村邑：以大隊騎兵沿山道與河谷推進，前鋒以弓矢覆蓋道路，逼迫對手結陣；一旦敵軍隊形鬆動或側翼暴露，便以密集箭雨衝擊其側後，然後迅速拉開，誘使追兵脫離本陣，再在選定地形上回身反擊。這套「擊而即走、走而再擊」的草原打法，重點在分散與縱深：各部以數百人為單位分別紮營，不給對手合圍的機會，戰利品就地分配，因此很難被一次殲滅。巴克特里亞一方的應對則以弓騎為骨幹：以巴克特里亞弓騎（希羅多德記載其步兵持短矛與蘆杆式斯基泰弓，騎兵用弓與標槍）覆蓋機動，集結重裝騎兵擔任衝鋒與追擊，把來敵引入河谷與隘口，利用地形切斷其退路，並以城與堡壘作為消耗戰的支點。必須說明的是，卡面這件亞述長弓所代表的那套「成排齊射、車步協同」的亞述戰術，在公元前一六二年早已不復存在；當年真正決定戰局的，是遊牧式的單騎散射與希臘化方面的混合兵種，這正是兩個軍事體系在亞述時代之後分道揚鑣的地方。
tacticsEn: The two tactical systems were almost the opposite of one another. The Saka did not attack walls and did not seek to hold cities; their thrust was aimed at pastures and villages. They advanced in great bodies of horse along the mountain tracks and river valleys, the leading rank covering the road with arrows and forcing the enemy to form up; the moment an enemy formation slackened or a flank opened, they would strike it with a dense arrow-fall from the side and rear, then break away at once, lure the pursuers out of their order, and turn again on ground of their own choosing. This grassland way of hitting and then withdrawing, withdrawing and hitting again, put its weight on dispersion and depth: each tribe encamped separately in units of several hundred, so that no encirclement was possible, and the spoil was divided on the spot, which is why a single blow rarely destroyed them. The Bactrian answer was built on the mass of mounted archers. Bactrian horse archers covered the manoeuvre, with the heavy cavalry massed for the charge and the pursuit, drawing the enemy into the river valleys and the defiles so as to cut off the retreat, and the cities and forts were used as the anchor of a war of attrition. It must be said that the tactical system the Assyrian bow on the card stands for, the volley fire in ranks combined with chariot and infantry, was already long gone by 162 BC. What decided the fighting in that year was the nomadic style of individual shooting on horseback against the mixed arms of the Hellenistic states, and that is precisely where the two military systems parted company after the age of Assyria.
data: 本戰可核對的數字極少，這本身即是這場戰爭的特點：所有涉及公元前一六二年那一次入侵的古典記載，都沒有留下兵員、俘虜、戰損或掠奪物的數目。可以引為旁證的，是歐克拉提德王朝的錢幣與幾項可測的數據：歐克拉提德所鑄的二十斯塔特金幣約重一百六十九克，是已知最大的古代金幣，現藏大英博物館；亞伊哈努姆出土的一枚銀章約重二百克，學界據其銘文把歐克拉提德即位的年代定在公元前一七〇年前後；另有年代學界仍有爭議的希臘化巴克特里亞王陵金器出土於泰利亞泰佩。希臘化巴克特里亞的兵力規模，在亞歷山大時代的記載中可見一斑：巴克特里亞可出騎兵三萬，格拉尼庫斯河戰役中該國出兵二千騎。漢籍方面，張騫報告大夏「城邑數百」「控弦者二十餘萬」「人口百餘萬」，又記大月氏「戶十餘萬」而「控弦之士十餘萬」「騎兵十餘萬」，這些數目大致對應公元前一二世紀中亞草原聯盟的規模。距離可以估算：巴克特拉到亞伊哈努姆約四百公里，自伊犁河谷經天山通道抵扎拉夫尚河谷約七百至九百公里。傷亡數字：無記載。月份方面史無所載，填四月只是依巴克特里亞春末用兵與遊牧春夏牧場期的季節所作的推測。
dataEn: Very little about this war can be checked numerically, and that is itself a feature of it: no classical account of the incursion of 162 BC gives any figure for men, prisoners, losses or plunder. What can be used as corroboration comes from the coinage of the Eucratid dynasty and from a few measurable objects. The twenty-stater gold coin struck by Eucratides weighs about 169 grams and is the largest ancient gold coin known, now in the British Museum. A silver medallion found at Ai-Khanoum weighs about 200 grams, and its inscription has been used to date Eucratides' accession to around 170 BC. A gold hoard from a royal tomb of Hellenistic Bactria, whose dating is still disputed, came to light at Tillya Tepe. The military scale of Hellenistic Bactria can be seen in the accounts of Alexander's day: Bactria could put thirty thousand horsemen into the field, and supplied two thousand cavalry at the battle of the Granicus. On the Chinese side Zhang Qian reported of Daxia several hundred cities, more than two hundred thousand bowmen and a population of over a million, and of the Yuezhi more than a hundred thousand households, more than a hundred thousand bowmen and more than a hundred thousand horsemen; these figures roughly match the scale of the Central Asian steppe confederations of the first and second centuries BC. Distances can be estimated: about 400 kilometres from Bactra to Ai-Khanoum, and some seven to nine hundred kilometres from the Ili valley across the Tian Shan passes to the Zeravshan valley. Figures for losses: none. As for the month, the record is silent, and April is entered only as an inference from the season in which Bactria customarily took the field and from the spring and summer pastures of the nomads.
cause: 打起來的原因，可以拆成四層。最外的一層是草原的連鎖壓力：匈奴在公元前一七六年前後奪取河西走廊，大月氏被迫西遷至伊犁河谷，前132年又被烏孫逐出，遂再向南渡過阿姆河；他們在阿姆河上游遇到並逐走塞種，把塞種整體推向西南。第二層是塞種自身的處境：塞種原居於雅克薩特斯河以東至費爾干納、伊犁一帶，東面是天山，西面是帕提亞在米特里達特一世治下向北吞併的河中與索格底亞，南面正是巴克特里亞的門戶；當上游與側翼都被封住，剩下的出路只有向南。第三層是物質的誘因：扎拉夫尚河谷、蘇爾漢達利亞河谷與瓦罕的冬窩水草豐美，穀物、葡萄酒、鐵器與貴金屬齊備，而草原上的游牧部眾在歉歲時最需要這種穀物；更重要的是安提奧庫斯三世為防遊牧人而修築於雅克薩特斯河一線的長城，此時已被突破或失去功能，門戶洞開。第四層是希臘化巴克特里亞自身的內部問題：歐克拉提德十餘年前以政變奪權，需要把財力集中在王位與東征上，邊區總督與村社的抵抗未平，北面守備空虛，於是任何一股遊牧兵力的試探都可能引發全面進攻。公元前一六二年那一次入侵的直接導火線沒有留下記載，以上是由同期前後二十年的材料歸納出的通例。
causeEn: The reasons can be taken apart into four layers. The outermost is the chain of pressure coming out of the steppe: the Xiongnu took the Hexi Corridor shortly before 176 BC, the Yuezhi were driven west to the Ili valley, and in 132 BC they were driven out of the Ili valley by the Wusun, so they moved south again across the Oxus; on the north bank of that river they met and expelled the Saka, pushing the Saka bodily to the south-west. The second layer is the Saka's own position: their homeland lay from beyond the Jaxartes as far as Ferghana and the Ili, with the Tian Shan to the east, the lands of the Oxus and Sogdiana absorbed to the west by Parthia under Mithridates I, and the door into Bactria to the south. With the upper flank and the side closed off, the only road left was southward. The third layer is material inducement: the Zeravshan valley, the Surkhan Darya valley and the winter quarters of Wakhsh offered good grass, and grain, wine, iron and precious metal were to be had, while the nomadic groups of the steppe needed that grain most in a poor year. More importantly, the great wall that Antiochus III had built along the Jaxartes to hold the nomads back had by now been broken or rendered useless, and the door stood open. The fourth layer is the internal condition of Hellenistic Bactria itself: Eucratides had taken the throne by coup a dozen years earlier, the state's resources were being concentrated on the crown and on the campaigns in India, the resistance of the provincial satraps and village communities had not been settled, and the northern defence was thin; so any probe by a nomadic force could turn into a full invasion. The immediate trigger of the incursion of 162 BC left no record, and what is set out above is a generalisation drawn from the material of the twenty years before and after.
impact: 影響可以分對內與對外兩面。對內，這一場入侵把巴克特里亞王國的北界從蘇爾漢達利亞上游與阿姆河一線硬生生推到扎拉夫尚河谷與巴克特拉一線，歐克拉提德王朝原有的東部衛星國與邊境要塞體系失效，前線自此長期暴露在草原壓力之下；此後約前140年塞種大舉南侵帕提亞，殺死弗拉阿特斯二世並擊潰其希臘傭兵，前145年亞伊哈努姆在遊牧入侵中被焚而再未重建，前125年前後巴克特拉淪陷，希臘化巴克特里亞王國就此終結，殘部南撤並以喀布爾河谷為中心建立印度—希臘王國。對外，這是希臘化世界第一次被中亞草原力量正面推倒一個王國，隨後大月氏越過阿姆河定居巴克特里亞並逐漸希臘化，漢朝於是並列大夏、安息、康居、大月氏為西域要國，東段絲路的安全從此成為漢廷的長期關切。作戰層面上的影響同樣深遠：定居國家被迫放棄亞述時代那種純粹靠弓兵齊射的兵種結構，轉向以重裝騎兵、弓騎混編與城防為核心的體系，這一取向在後來的印度—帕提亞與印度—西徐亞戰爭中定型；而以弓為主的草原射術與騎射戰法，也在這一時期反過來傳入中亞定居國家，改變了東方的兵學。
impactEn: The consequences divide into the internal and the external. Internally, this incursion pushed the northern boundary of the Bactrian kingdom hard back from the upper Surkhan Darya and the line of the Oxus to the Zeravshan valley and Bactra. The system of eastern client states and frontier fortresses that had belonged to the Eucratid dynasty stopped functioning, and the front line was left from that point on exposed to pressure from the steppe. Around 140 BC the Saka struck deep into Parthia, killing Phraates II and routing his Greek mercenaries; around 145 BC Ai-Khanoum was burned in a nomadic raid and was never rebuilt; around 125 BC Bactra fell, and with it the Hellenistic kingdom of Bactria came to an end, the survivors withdrawing south and setting up the Indo-Greek kingdom around the Kabul valley. Externally, this was the first time a Hellenistic state was openly overturned by the forces of the Central Asian steppe; the Yuezhi thereupon crossed the Oxus, settled in Bactria and were gradually Hellenised, and the Han court began to name Daxia, Anxi, Kangju and the Yuezhi together as the great states of the Western Regions, so that the security of the eastern section of the silk road became a standing concern of the Han government. The effect on the art of war was equally deep: the settled states were obliged to abandon the pure missile-first order of battle of the Assyrian age and to turn to a system built on cataphracts, mixed mounted and foot units, and fortification, an orientation that hardened in the later wars of the Indo-Parthians and the Indo-Scythians. At the same time the bow-centred grassland archery and the tactics of shooting from horseback passed back the other way into the Central Asian settled states and altered the military science of the East.
result: 結果可以分短期與長期。短期看，公元前一六二年這一次入侵並沒有留下可以核對的勝負記錄：古典作家只說希臘人一度把來敵逐出河谷，既無戰果數目，也沒有宣布征服或附庸化；可以確定的是，遊牧者的這次試探把希臘化巴克特里亞的注意力從印度戰線拉回北方，而北方恰恰是它守不住的方向。長期看，這場戰爭是巴克特里亞崩潰過程的起點而非終點：歐克拉提德約前145年死於自己人或地方總督之手，亞伊哈努姆同年被焚，希羅克拉底斯一世成為最後的希臘王，巴克特拉在約前125至前120年間失守，希臘化巴克特里亞王國亡於塞種與大月氏的先後南下。必須承認的是，這一場戰爭的直接記載極為貧乏，我們能確定的只有三件事：它發生在公元前一六二年前後的巴克特里亞東境；它屬於一個橫跨整個前二世紀的遷徙—入侵過程，而不是一次有明確勝負的會戰；它的詳細經過已隨同當時的記載一同散佚，今天能重建的，是它的模式，而不是它的戰況。
resultEn: The result divides into the short term and the long. In the short term, the incursion of 162 BC left behind no outcome that can be checked: the classical writers say only that the Greeks on one occasion drove the enemy back out of the valley, with no figure for the results and no announcement of conquest or of vassalage. What can be said with certainty is that this probe by the nomads pulled the attention of Hellenistic Bactria away from the Indian front and back to the north, which was precisely the direction it could not hold. In the long term this war was the beginning of the process of Bactria's collapse rather than its end. Eucratides was killed by one of his own men or by a provincial satrap around 145 BC, Ai-Khanoum was burned in the same year, Heliocles I became the last Greek king, and Bactra was lost some time between about 125 and 120 BC, the Hellenistic kingdom of Bactria perishing to the successive southward movement of the Saka and the Yuezhi. It must be admitted that the direct record of this war is very poor, and that only three things can be stated with certainty: it took place in the eastern part of Bactria around 162 BC; it belonged to a process of migration and invasion running across the whole of the second century BC rather than to a set-piece battle with a decided result; and its details are lost together with the documents of the time, so that what can be reconstructed today is its pattern and not its course.
